_comment: Per-provider text-language capabilities. Read by nodes/translate/_config.py exactly as speech_defaults.json is read by nodes/speech/_config.py: loaded once at import, every capability question answered from here, so no shared code branches on a provider name. Three capability blocks per provider — translate / transliterate / detect — and which blocks exist is advisory only; registry membership is the authority.
_common_languages_comment: Fallback for the language dropdowns when a provider does not declare a closed list. LLM-backed providers accept essentially any language, so this is a convenience shortlist rather than a constraint.

deepl._comment: Translation only — DeepL ships no transliteration or standalone language-ID product, so it registers into one registry and is unreachable from the other two nodes. That asymmetry is the reason this layer has three registries rather than one with capability flags.
deepl._free_base_url_comment: Free keys end in ':fx' and MUST use the api-free host; the pro host rejects them with 403. The provider picks the host from the key suffix, so a user never has to know which they hold.

translate._formality_comment: Only supported on some target languages; DeepL 400s on the rest, so 'prefer_' variants are the safe choice.
translate._languages_comment: Fetched live from /languages, which is authoritative and changes without notice. This list is only the cold-start fallback for the dropdown.
translate._billing_comment: DeepL returns billed_characters per translation, so the node reports the provider's own figure rather than counting input itself.

sarvam._comment: Indic-first, and the only provider here serving all three capabilities over dedicated REST endpoints. Ported from the retired sarvamTranslate / sarvamTransliterate / sarvamDetectLanguage nodes.

translate._max_input_comment: Enforced client-side so the LLM gets an actionable message instead of an opaque 422.
translate._languages_comment: sarvam-translate:v1 covers all 22; mayura:v1 covers the 10-language core plus English. The wider set is the default because the default model supports it.

openai._comment: LLM-backed rather than a dedicated translation API. Serves all three capabilities by prompting through ChatUnifier, which is why its billing unit is TOKENS, not characters — the ChatUnifier path already records token cost under llm.openai, so this layer records nothing and would otherwise double-count. Proves the Protocol does not care what a provider does internally.
